title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Determine Jurisdiction When the Name and Content of an Economic Contract Are Inconsistent

articles.content_en: 1. Where an economic contract signed by the parties has a definite and standardized name, but the rights and obligations stipulated in the contract are inconsistent with the name, the nature of the contract shall be determined based on the content of the rights and obligations stipulated in the contract, thereby determining the place of performance of the contract and the jurisdiction of the court.

2. Where the name of the contract is inconsistent with the content of the rights and obligations stipulated in the contract, and it is difficult to distinguish the nature of the contract based on the content of the rights and obligations stipulated in the contract, and the name of the contract is consistent with part of the rights and obligations stipulated in the contract, the place of performance of the contract and the jurisdiction of the court shall be determined based on the name of the contract.
November 13, 1996
